newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Jewish settlements have high rate of vacant homes.
newsitem.headline: Jewish settlements have high rate of vacant homes.

text.p: Jewish settlements on occupied Arab lands have a higher percent of vacant homes than inside Israel, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Tuesday.
In Israel, five percent of the housing stock was empty compared with 12.1 percent in Jewish settlements in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip.
At the Kiryat Arba settlement, on the outskirts of the Palestinian West Bank town of Hebron, long a flashpoint of Arab-Israeli violence, 18.5 percent of the homes stood vacant, the bureau said.

It based the figures on a census conducted in November 1995 that found there were 1.64 million residential units in Israel and in Jewish settlements. The bureau did not give a figure for the total number of housing units in settlements.

The report gave no reason for the low occupancy in settlements but under a framework interim peace deal reached between Israel and the Palestinians in September 1993 the fate of settlements was left for negotiation at final status talks.
The talks were to resume on Monday but did not amidst the controversy over Israel's internationally condemned decision to build a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. Work began on Tuesday.
More than 130,000 Jews have settled among some two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip since Israel occupied the areas in the 1967 Middle East war.
